Heart of Christ
hart uv kryst
noun phrase (the disposition of the Saviour)
From the biblical use of “heart” for the seat of disposition and affection; the settled disposition of the Lord Jesus toward sinners and saints, revealed chiefly in His own word, “meek and lowly in heart.”

📖 Biblical Definition

The heart of Christ is the settled disposition and affection of the Lord Jesus toward sinners who come to Him, revealed supremely in His own self-description: “I am meek and lowly in heart.” It is the one place in the Gospels where the Lord lifts the veil upon His inmost disposition, and what He shows is not severity but gentleness toward the weary and heavy laden. The Gospels display this heart at every turn: He was moved with compassion on the multitudes, for they fainted and were scattered as sheep having no shepherd; He wept at the grave of Lazarus and over Jerusalem; He received sinners and ate with them. As a great High Priest He is touched with the feeling of our infirmities, having been tempted in all points like as we are, yet without sin, so that He is no distant deity but a sympathizing Saviour who knows our frame. Having loved His own which were in the world, He loved them unto the end. The dictionary marks the heart of Christ against a doubled error: the legalism that pictures a grudging Saviour who must be coaxed to mercy, and the sentimentality that makes His love an indulgent permissiveness blind to sin. The true heart of Christ is gentle and lowly toward the broken, fierce against hypocrisy, holy in all its tenderness; He casts out none that come, yet calls all who come to repentance, and His compassion is the very compassion of God toward His own.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The settled disposition of the Lord Jesus toward sinners—“meek and lowly in heart”—displayed in His compassion, His sympathy as High Priest, and His love unto the end; gentle toward the broken yet holy in all its tenderness.

HEART OF CHRIST, noun phrase. The inmost disposition and affection of the Lord Jesus toward His people.

Revealed in His own word: “I am meek and lowly in heart” (Matthew 11:29).

Displayed in His compassion on the shepherdless multitudes (Matthew 9:36).

As High Priest, touched with the feeling of our infirmities (Hebrews 4:15).

Gentle toward the broken, fierce against hypocrisy, holy in all its tenderness.

📖 Key Scripture

Mt 11:29 — "Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls."

Mt 9:36 — "But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd."

Heb 4:15 — "For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin."

Joh 13:1 — "Now before the feast of the passover, when Jesus knew that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The legalist makes Christ's heart grudging and severe; the sentimentalist makes it an indulgent permissiveness blind to sin—both lose the gentle, holy compassion the Gospels reveal.

expand to see more

One corruption pictures a reluctant Saviour, His heart a closed fist that must be pried open by tears and merit, as though the Father were eager to save but the Son must be persuaded. Scripture overturns this: the Son says of Himself that He is meek and lowly in heart, and that he that cometh to Him He will in no wise cast out. The dictionary recovers the truth that the gentleness of Christ is not earned but freely given, the very disposition of His being toward sinners who come.

The opposite and more fashionable corruption melts the heart of Christ into mere sentiment—an affirming, indulgent love that overlooks sin and asks nothing of repentance. But the same Lord who was moved with compassion drove the money-changers from the temple, denounced the hypocrites with woes, and called sinners to forsake their sin. His tenderness is holy: He receives the broken and the penitent, not the proud and the impenitent. The dictionary holds both together—a heart genuinely gentle toward the weary and heavy laden, and genuinely holy, that loves sinners too much to leave them in their sin.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the biblical leb (Hebrew) and kardia (Greek), the heart as the seat of thought, will, and affection; Christ's “lowly in heart” (Greek tapeinos te kardia) names His inmost disposition.

expand to see more

Kardia, Greek, the heart as the centre of disposition, will, and affection.

Tapeinos, Greek, lowly or humble, joined to “heart” in Matthew 11:29.

Splanchnizomai, Greek, “moved with compassion,” literally yearning in the inward parts.

Sumpatheo, Greek, to be touched with feeling, of the sympathizing High Priest (Hebrews 4:15).

Eis telos, Greek, “unto the end,” the constancy of His love (John 13:1).

Usage

"The pastor preached the heart of Christ to weary believers, that the Saviour is meek and lowly and casts out none who come."

"He warned against a sentimental Jesus, for the same gentle heart drove the traffickers from His Father's house."

"She drew near with boldness, knowing the High Priest is touched with the feeling of her infirmities."
